emergence and global spread of new delhi metallo β lactamase 1 ndm 1 pose a severe threat to the efficacy of carbapenems which are considered the last line of defense against infections caused by multidrug resistant gram negative bacteria in this study through virtual screening and enzyme activity inhibition assays phthalylsulfacetamide psa was identified as a compound exhibiting inhibitory activity against ndm 1 psa dose dependently inhibited ndm 1 with a 50 inhibitory concentration ic 50 of 15 4 0 3 μm and an inhibition rate ir of 89 2 in vitro antibacterial activity assays confirmed that psa effectively restored the antibacterial activity of meropenem mem against ndm 1 positive escherichia coli e coli reducing the minimum inhibitory concentration mic of mem by 32 fold and demonstrating rapid bactericidal effects within 3 h the combination of psa and mem had a significant synergistic effect with a fractional inhibitory concentration index fici of 0 156 in vivo the combination therapy significantly reduced the bacterial load decreased inflammatory cytokine levels alleviated histopathological damage and increased survival rates in a murine systemic infection model molecular dynamics simulation and site directed mutagenesis revealed that psa stably binds to the active hydrolysis center of ndm 1 interacts with zn 2 and strongly interacts with the key amino acid residues val73 and his122 furthermore the observed rapid bactericidal activity suggests that psa s mechanism of action may extend beyond ndm 1 inhibition molecular docking analysis indicates that psa may potentially interact with lpxc a key enzyme involved in lipopolysaccharide synthesis however this observation remains preliminary and requires further experimental validation these results highlight psa as a promising therapeutic agent against ndm 1 mediated carbapenem resistance graphical abstract keywords phthalylsulfacetamide ndm 1 carbapenem resistance inhibitor synergistic effect biomed central ltd part of springer nature 2026 introduction the discovery and use of β lactam antibiotics played an irreplaceable role in the prevention and treatment of bacterial infections and was hailed as a major contribution to the history of medicine in the past century 1 β lactam antibiotics have been the most widely used antibacterial drugs in medicine and animal breeding since they were developed and their utilization rate in the worldwide antibiotic market is greater than 65 2 penicillin and cephalosporins are the most commonly used first line drugs for the treatment of drug resistant escherichia coli e coli infection in veterinary clinics 3 carbapenems such as meropenem mem are known as the last line of defense for treating multidrug resistant enterobacteriaceae infections and are listed as highly important antibacterial drugs for human medicine by the world health organization who 4 no country in the world has approved the use of mem in animals but many animal derived carbapenem resistant e coli strains have emerged posing a great challenge to the treatment of colibacillosis 5 6 β lactamases bls secreted by bacteria can efficiently hydrolyze a variety of β lactam antibiotics which is the main mechanism of β lactam antibiotic failure and bacterial drug resistance 7 bls can be divided into serine β lactamases sbls and metallo β lactamases mbls according to their different amino acid sequences and mechanisms 8 among the mechanisms causing gram negative bacterial infections subclass b1 mbls have become the number one threat to clinical β lactam antibiotic therapy because of their extensive hydrolysis substrate profile among which new delhi metallo β lactamase 1 ndm 1 is the most concerning 9 11 bacteria expressing ndm 1 can stably and efficiently hydrolyze all β lactam antibiotics except monocyclic antibiotics including broad spectrum cephalosporins and carbapenems 12 further research revealed that bla ndm 1 was localized on inca c incf incx 1 and other plasmids and could spread and transfer among different bacteria and strains mainly e coli acinetobacter baumannii and klebsiella pneumoniae 13 the bla ndm 1 can even spread rapidly among animals the environment and humans through biological media 14 selective pressure from antibiotic overuse continues to drive the evolution of ndm 1 with over 40 variants identified 15 bacteria that produce the ndm 1 enzyme are called superbugs because of their extensive drug resistance and transmission risk to combat these superdrug resistant bacteria the development of new antibiotics or antibiotic alternatives is urgently needed 16 17 however the development of new antibiotics is hindered by several disadvantages including high costs extended timelines and a significant rate of rediscovery 18 19 this challenge is particularly pronounced for gram negative bacteria which possess outer membrane permeability barriers that complicate the development of effective new antibiotics 20 in comparison the development of new mbl inhibitors that target resistance mechanisms combined with β lactam antibiotics presents a low cost safe and efficient approach to enhance the antibacterial activity of existing antibiotics 21 this strategy is currently among the most effective methods for addressing superbug infections 22 among antibacterial synergists sbl inhibitors have been more successfully studied at present the sbl inhibitors approved by the fda include clavulanic acid sulbactam and tazobactam 23 unlike sbls mbls are zinc ion dependent enzymes that cannot be inhibited by sbls inhibitor 24 owing to the lack of effective ndm 1 inhibitors for clinical use screening for specific ndm 1 enzyme inhibitors is essential for the treatment of multidrug resistant gram negative bacterial infections virtual screening based on molecular docking is a method that simulates and computationally evaluates the interactions between the three dimensional structure of target proteins and small molecules it assesses the binding affinity and conformation of various compounds with the target protein to identify potential active candidates the process mainly involves receptor modeling preprocessing of the small molecule library docking and scoring and post processing of hit compounds with docking and scoring being the core steps in this study the glide module of the schrödinger software was employed for docking this module is characterized by fast processing speed and high accuracy providing reliable support for the efficient discovery of novel ndm 1 inhibitors 25 from a diverse ligand compound library phthalylsulfacetamide psa was identified as a promising candidate psa is a broad spectrum bacteriostatic agent classified as a sulfonamide 26 upon oral administration psa is decomposed in the intestine resulting in an antibacterial effect 27 this agent exhibits therapeutic efficacy against both gram positive and gram negative bacterial infections clinically psa is primarily utilized for the treatment of bacillary dysentery and diarrhea and for the prevention of infections before and after enteritis and intestinal surgery 26 this study aimed to discover novel ndm 1 inhibitors targeting its zinc active site using computational screening psa was identified as an effective ndm 1 inhibitor demonstrating synergistic antibacterial activity with mem in vitro and in vivo and its mechanism was elucidated this work provides a potential strategy and foundation for developing specific inhibitors against ndm 1 mediated resistance and treating drug resistant bacterial infections materials and methods molecular docking the crystal structure of an ndm 1 ligand complex expressed in e coli was retrieved from the protein data bank pdb https www rcsb org pdb id 4ey2 as the initial structure for molecular docking small molecule ligands were selected from the bioactive compound library target mol usa both the ndm 1 protein structure and the small molecule compounds were preprocessed using the glide module within the schrödinger software package importantly the zn² ions present in the crystal structure were retained during protein preparation and their coordination geometry was preserved as defined in the original structure during receptor grid generation the docking site was centered on the zn² containing active site to ensure appropriate sampling of ligands capable of interacting with the metal center in the glide docking protocol the zn² ion was treated as an integral part of the receptor allowing potential metal ligand coordination interactions to be considered during scoring semiflexible docking was then performed between ndm 1 and the ligand library using the glide and maestro modules potential ndm 1 inhibitors were identified on the basis of docking scores g scores representing semiempirical binding free energy and compliance with lipinski s rule of five for drug like the stability of the psa ndm 1 complex and elucidated the molecular mechanism of psa mediated ndm 1 inhibition through competitive active site binding discussion the global spread of ndm 1 producing enterobacteriaceae which renders carbapenems ineffective is a critical public health challenge 31 in this context our study identifies phthalylsulfacetamide psa as a potent ndm 1 inhibitor capable of restoring mem activity the repurposing of psa an already approved and safe drug offers a distinct advantage over de novo drug development by significantly accelerating translational timelines 32 this strategy holds immediate promise for veterinary medicine where carbapenem resistant e coli in livestock presents serious zoonotic risks 33 our findings suggest that psa mem combinations can be swiftly deployed in the veterinary field to control ndm 1 positive infections effectively mitigating the risk of resistance transfer to human populations our study demonstrated that psa exhibited remarkable synergistic effects with meropenem against ndm 1 positive e coli reducing the mic of meropenem by 32 fold with a fici of 0 156 this level of synergy surpasses those reported for other metallo β lactamase mbl inhibitors such as aspergillomarasmine a and edta derivatives 34 in addition the in vivo efficacy of the combination was particularly striking achieving 70 survival in lethal infection models compared with 20 in controls accompanied by a reduced bacterial load and decreased proinflammatory cytokine levels in summary the potent synergistic bactericidal effect observed for the psa and mem combination highlights the significant potential of psa as an mem adjuvant importantly psa demonstrated an excellent safety profile with no observable cytotoxicity at therapeutic doses addressing a key limitation of currently available metalloenzyme inhibitors 35 although psa exhibited limited intrinsic antibacterial activity in vitro its potential contribution particularly in the intestinal environment where it may be converted into sulfacetamide cannot be completely excluded and may partially contribute to the observed in vivo effects md simulations provided crucial insights into the structural basis of psa inhibitory activity the observed stable binding conformation and favorable binding free energy demonstrate the high affinity of psa for the ndm 1 active site notably our mutagenesis studies revealed val73 and his122 as critical residues for psa binding with alanine substitutions at these positions resulting in reduced inhibitory efficacy this mechanism differs significantly from that of zinc chelating compounds such as edta highlighting the unique residue specific interactions of psa that could lead to improved selectivity and reduced off target effects 36 37 from a structural perspective the identification of val73 and his122 as critical binding residues provides valuable insights for rational drug design these residues are conserved across many ndm variants suggesting that psa derivatives can maintain activity against diverse ndm mutants future studies should explore the structure activity relationships to optimize psa potency while maintaining its favorable safety profile 38 40 while the primary and experimentally supported mechanism of psa involves the inhibition of ndm 1 its rapid bactericidal effect observed within 3 h in the time kill assays suggests that additional mechanisms may be involved molecular docking analysis suggests that psa may potentially interact with lpxc a key enzyme involved in lipid a biosynthesis 41 if validated this interaction could contribute to disruption of the bacterial outer membrane and facilitate antibiotic penetration 42 43 however this proposed mechanism remains speculative and requires further experimental validation therefore the potential involvement of lpxc should be interpreted with caution although the application prospect of psa is broad there are still limitations in this study that need to be addressed first the spectrum of pathogens including other mbls such as vim and imp that can be inhibited by psa remains unknown in addition only a single ndm 1 positive e coli strain was evaluated in this study although the results demonstrate a strong synergistic effect validation across multiple clinical isolates is necessary to confirm the general applicability of psa as an ndm 1 inhibitor another limitation is that the pharmacokinetic synergy with mem needs optimization as the subcutaneous administration of mem and the oral administration of psa may lead to mismatched tissue distribution it is important to note that the identified optimal mem psa ratio of 1 2 is based on a comparison within a predefined clinically relevant dose range future studies involving more extensive dose ranging and pharmacokinetic pharmacodynamic modeling are warranted to refine the optimal ratio for potential clinical application future studies should explore psa derivatives with enhanced blood brain barrier penetration for systemic infections 44 conclusion in conclusion this study confirms that psa acts as a potent and specific inhibitor of ndm 1 effectively restoring mem susceptibility in ndm 1 positive e coli through competitive binding to the ndm 1 active site the psa and mem combination demonstrated notable synergistic effects both in vitro and in vivo significantly reducing bacterial load alleviating histopathological damage and increasing survival rates these results highlight the potential of psa as a therapeutic adjuvant against carbapenem resistant infections further clinical studies are warranted to translate these findings into practical applications publisher s note springer nature remains neutral with regard to jurisdictional
